newsitem.title: USA: Georgia asks for share of any tobacco settlement.
newsitem.headline: Georgia asks for share of any tobacco settlement.

text.p: The state of Georgia has sent letters asking Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp for a share of any possible settlement of lawsuits against the tobacco companies, a governor's spokeswoman said Thursday.
The state of Georgia is not one of the more than 20 states that has filed lawsuits against cigarette manufacturers to recoup Medicaid costs for treating smokers.

"In the event of a settlement of the current tobacco litigation with the litigating states, the state of Georgia expects to receive no less favorable treatment in resolving any simular claims that may be available to Georgia against the tobacco companies," the letters said.
The letters, addressed to the two companies' chairmen and signed by Gov. Zell Miller and Attorney General Michael Bowers, were dated Wednesday, April 30.
